model.name: Evidence / Rationale
model.purpose: Traceable support for a claim or decision
model.scope_statement: This mixin attaches a format-neutral evidence-and-rationale record to a host knowledge object, claim, decision, finding, credential, or similar assertion. It covers the identity of a support record, the support relation to a fact or decision of consequence, documented reasons, relevance and certainty, authenticity and integrity, chain of custody, handling lifecycle, stewardship, access constraints, and citations or selectors. It does not own the host proposition, the legal proceeding, the scientific study protocol, or a general provenance graph.
in_scope: Identity, classification, and versioning of an evidence or rationale record that can be mixed into a host entity.
The support relation between an evidence item or rationale and a claim, decision, fact of consequence, credential, or recommendation.
Documented reasons, motivations, judgment footnotes, and evidence-to-decision considerations that explain why a claim or decision is supported.
Relevance, certainty or quality rating, quantitative statistics, and other weight signals that a consumer uses to rely on the support.
Authentication that an item is what it is claimed to be, content-integrity bindings, and chain-of-custody chronology.
Handling states from identification, collection, acquisition and preservation through review, challenge, invalidation, sealing, redaction, retention and deletion.
Stewardship, authorship, issuance, custody, endorsement, access, privilege, disclosure minimization, and interoperability with related artifacts and selectors.
out_of_scope: The host knowledge proposition, claim text, or decision act itself, which belong to Knowledge (WM-KNW-008) and any sibling Decision or Claim models.
A general provenance graph of entities, activities and agents as a first-class world model; this mixin may reference provenance but does not replace W3C PROV.
Cryptographic securing mechanisms, proofs and signatures used to protect a credential or manifest, which W3C Verifiable Credentials distinguish from evidence.
Court docketing, hearing calendars, jury instructions, and other proceeding-management records.
Forensic laboratory competence systems, tool validation programmes, and physical evidence-warehouse logistics as operational systems.
Scientific study protocol, population definition, and evidence-variable catalogues as first-class research objects, except as referenced support.
Argument-dialogue games, agent negotiation protocols, and a canonical Toulmin or Argument Interchange Format graph, which lack a governing primary alignment in this research.

boundary_notes.distinction: Knowledge is the host proposition, finding or recorded knowing. This mixin supplies traceable support and reasons for that host; it is not itself the claim being known.

PROV records how entities were generated, used, derived and attributed, including provenance of provenance via bundles. Evidence uses those facts to support a claim or decision; a derivation trail is not by itself a relevance or certainty judgment.
A verifiable credential expresses issuer claims about a subject. The evidence property carries supporting information for those claims and is explicitly different from securing mechanisms and proofs.

An annotation associates a body with a target for a motivation such as commenting or assessing. Evidential support may be projected as an annotation, but annotation motivation is not equivalent to relevance, custody or certainty of evidence.

C2PA binds signed assertions about origin and edits to an asset and refuses value judgments about whether provenance is good or bad. Those assertions may be cited as support; they do not decide the truth of a depicted event or the merits of a decision.

Federal Rules 401 and 901 define relevance and authentication as legal tests applied by a proponent and trier. This mixin records the characteristics those tests inspect; it does not perform a ruling, admit an exhibit, or manage a case.

ISO/IEC 27037 and NIST SP 800-86 govern identification, collection, acquisition, preservation and incident-oriented forensic process. This mixin records handling and custody facts needed to rely on an item; it is not a forensic-capability or incident-response system.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.relevance: Defines provenance as information about entities, activities and agents used to assess quality, reliability or trustworthiness, including derivation, responsibility, time, collections and provenance-of-provenance bundles needed when evidence itself must be justified.

sources.title: FHIR Resource Evidence
sources.relevance: Machine-interpretable evidence record with identifiers, status lifecycle, authors, reviewers, endorsers, description, assertion, notes, related artifacts, statistics, study and synthesis types, and a certainty element for overall and subcomponent quality.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: Normative evidence property for supporting information attached to a claim, with optional id, required type, optional name, description and content digest, and an explicit distinction between evidence and cryptographic securing mechanisms.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model
sources.relevance: Body-target association with motivation and purpose as the why of a statement, lifecycle and agent properties, rights, and selectors that pinpoint the portion of a resource offered as support.

sources.title: Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 401. Test for Relevant Evidence
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
sources.relevance: Defines relevance as a relation: evidence is relevant only if it tends to make a fact of consequence more or less probable. Relevancy is not an inherent property of an item.

sources.title: Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 901. Authenticating or Identifying Evidence
sources.organization: Supreme Court of the United States
sources.relevance: Requires the proponent to produce support sufficient to find that an item is what it is claimed to be, including witness knowledge, distinctive characteristics, public records, process or system accuracy, and other non-exclusive methods.

sources.title: GRADE Working Group: What is GRADE?
sources.version_or_date: minimal GRADE requirements updated 2023-05; site accessed 2026-08-23
sources.relevance: Normative certainty-of-evidence method with explicit domains, four-level ratings, evidence tables, and Evidence to Decision criteria that require documented judgments and the evidence informing each criterion.

sources.title: Content Credentials: C2PA Technical Specification
sources.organization: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
sources.relevance: Tamper-evident manifests binding hashed assertions, claims, signatures and timestamps to assets, with validation states, redaction, unique identifiers and an explicit refusal to judge provenance as good or bad.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-86 Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques into Incident Response
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Forensic process guidance for collecting, examining and analyzing digital sources while preserving integrity for later reliance, from an IT and incident-response view rather than a law-enforcement view.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 27037:2012 Information technology — Security techniques — Guidelines for identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of digital evidence
sources.relevance: International guidelines for identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of potential digital evidence of evidential value, including cross-jurisdiction exchange of potential evidence.

bundles.name: Identity and support relation
bundles.description: Who or what the evidence or rationale record is, how it is classified, and which host claim, decision or fact of consequence it is offered to support.
bundles.rationale: Relevance exists only as a relation between an item and a matter of consequence, and both FHIR Evidence and Verifiable Credentials identify a support record separately from the host assertion.

layers.name: Support-record identity
layers.description: Stable identifiers, titles, versions and host binding for an evidence or rationale instance.

findings.name: Evidence or rationale record identity
findings.description: An evidence or rationale record needs a master identifier, optional global IRI, human title, business version and record type so agents can cite, compare and mix it into a host without treating a date as an identifier.

questions.text: What authoritative master-system identifier, governed IRI, or Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID identifies this evidence or rationale record?
What human title, machine name and typed class distinguish this record as evidence, rationale, or a typed subtype such as a credential evidence object or FHIR Evidence resource?
What business version and version-comparison method apply, and when was the record last changed as distinct from when the underlying event occurred?

data_elements.name: Master identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier assigned by the governing system of record for this evidence or rationale instance.

data_elements.name: Global IRI
data_elements.description: Optional dereferenceable or governed IRI for the record, following identifier practice in Verifiable Credentials and C2PA manifests.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Fallback unique identifier assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or IRI exists.

data_elements.name: Record type
data_elements.description: Required type of the evidence object or evidence resource class.

data_elements.name: Title
data_elements.description: Human-friendly name of the evidence or summary.

data_elements.name: Business version
data_elements.description: Business version of the evidence summary or support record.

data_elements.name: Last changed at
data_elements.description: Observation or last-changed timestamp of the support record in RFC 3339, not used as an identifier.

artifacts.name: Evidence record header
artifacts.description: Canonical identity document or header for the support record, independent of storage format.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the master identifier, else the global IRI, else a Dimension UUID or ULID; never a date.

findings.name: Supported target and support relation
findings.description: Evidence is relevant only relative to a fact of consequence or host claim. The mixin must name the host, the fact or decision supported, the polarity of support, and whether the support is offered, admitted, or merely cited.

questions.text: Which host knowledge object, claim, decision, credential or finding does this record support, and under what identifier?
What fact of consequence, assertion or decision criterion is the evidence directed to, and is that fact ultimate, intermediate or background?
Does the item tend to increase or decrease the probability of that fact, and is the relation one of support, citation, annotation body-to-target, or related-artifact linkage?

data_elements.name: Host reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the host entity receiving this mixin.

data_elements.name: Fact of consequence
data_elements.description: The matter to which proof or support is directed; need not be disputed.

data_elements.name: Support polarity
data_elements.description: Whether the item makes the fact more probable, less probable, or is offered as background.

data_elements.name: Relation type
data_elements.description: Typed link such as related artifact, annotation target, or credential evidence attachment.

data_elements.name: Assertion text
data_elements.description: Declarative description of what the evidence is taken to show.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The support relation is reference data linking a host to a fact of consequence; it has no independent exhibit unless a covering sheet is later compiled.

layers.name: Evidence classification
layers.description: Typed kind and form of the support, distinct from the host and from cryptographic proofs.

findings.name: Evidence kind and form
findings.description: Classifies the support as documentary, testimonial, statistical, computational, physical-digital acquisition, or other typed evidence, and records whether it is an inline description, an external artifact, or a digest-bound file.

questions.text: What typed kind of evidence is this, using the governing type system of the host ecosystem?
Is this supporting information for a claim, or a cryptographic securing mechanism that must not be stored as evidence?
Is the support inline text, an external resource, an embedded binary, or a digest-addressed artifact, and what media or device class produced it?

data_elements.name: Evidence kind
data_elements.description: Required type of evidence information, as in Verifiable Credentials evidence objects.

data_elements.name: Form
data_elements.description: Inline, external, embedded or digest-bound form of the support.

data_elements.name: Media type
data_elements.description: Media or content type of an external or embedded evidence item.

data_elements.name: Device or source class
data_elements.description: Indicative class of digital source such as storage media, mobile device, camera or network, as scoped by ISO/IEC 27037.

data_elements.name: Is securing mechanism
data_elements.description: Flag that the item is a proof or signature and therefore out of this mixin.

artifacts.name: Typed evidence object
artifacts.description: Typed evidence payload, for example a VC evidence object pointing at an external file with a digest.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use evidence object id if present, else digest plus host credential id.

bundles.name: Rationale and documented inference
bundles.description: The why of a claim or decision: motivations, narrative reasons, judgment footnotes, and evidence-to-decision considerations, including recorded opposing considerations.
bundles.rationale: GRADE requires explicit documented rationale for certainty and recommendation judgments; Web Annotation models motivation as the why rather than who or when; FHIR provides description, assertion and notes for human-readable reasons.

layers.name: Documented reasons
layers.description: Narrative rationale, motivation, purpose and structured judgment notes.

findings.name: Rationale narrative and motivation
findings.description: Captures why the support was created or attached: motivation or purpose, primary description, interpretive assertion, and explanatory notes.

questions.text: What motivation or purpose explains why this rationale or annotation of support was created?
What is the primary human-readable description of the support and any interpretive assertion of what it shows?
What footnotes, variant comments or additional considerations must remain attached to the rationale?

data_elements.name: Motivation
data_elements.description: Reason for creating the support association, such as assessing, commenting or describing.

data_elements.name: Purpose
data_elements.description: Reason a particular body or note is included in the support record.

data_elements.name: Description
data_elements.description: Primary human-readable expression of the evidence or rationale.

data_elements.name: Assertion
data_elements.description: Interpretive declarative description of the evidence.

data_elements.name: Notes
data_elements.description: Footnotes and explanatory notes.

artifacts.name: Rationale memo
artifacts.description: Optional written rationale or opinion explaining the support in prose.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master rationale identifier plus monotonic serial for successive memos.

findings.name: Evidence-to-decision judgments
findings.description: Structured criteria and documented judgments that turn a body of evidence into a recommendation or decision, including the evidence informing each criterion.

questions.text: Which explicit health, contextual or other Evidence to Decision criteria were judged, and which were added for this decision type?
What judgment was recorded for each chosen criterion and which evidence informed that judgment?
If a recommendation was issued, what strength and direction were assigned using definitions consistent with the governing method?

data_elements.name: EtD criteria
data_elements.description: Explicit criteria forming the basis of the recommendation or decision.

data_elements.name: Criterion judgment
data_elements.description: Documented judgment for a criterion, with accessible additional considerations.

data_elements.name: Recommendation strength
data_elements.description: Strong or conditional strength if a recommendation is made.

data_elements.name: Recommendation direction
data_elements.description: For or against the option considered.

artifacts.name: Evidence to Decision framework record
artifacts.description: Structured EtD or equivalent judgment table with accessible rationale.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision identifier plus framework version and judgment-round serial.

layers.name: Opposing considerations
layers.description: Recorded residual opposing bias, undesirable effects and other considerations that count against the supported claim or option.

findings.name: Rebuttal and opposing considerations
findings.description: GRADE requires consideration of residual plausible opposing bias and both desirable and undesirable effects. A support record that cannot point to opposing considerations is incomplete for decision use.

questions.text: What residual opposing bias, harms, undesirable effects or contrary notes were explicitly considered?
Were both desirable and undesirable effects of the options described, with values and certainty?
What additional considerations that influenced the recommendation or decision were documented and made accessible?

data_elements.name: Opposing considerations
data_elements.description: Documented contrary or residual opposing factors.

data_elements.name: Undesirable effects
data_elements.description: Documented harms or undesirable health or other effects.

data_elements.name: Additional considerations
data_elements.description: Further influences on the recommendation that must remain accessible.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Opposing considerations are structured notes and criterion judgments stored with the EtD record; they do not require a separate exhibit type.

bundles.name: Relevance, certainty and weight
bundles.description: Signals a consumer uses to decide how far to rely on the support: relevance to a fact of consequence, GRADE-style certainty, and quantitative statistics.
bundles.rationale: Rule 401 separates relevance from sufficiency; GRADE and FHIR separate certainty rating from the statistic itself. These must not be collapsed into a single score.

layers.name: Relevance
layers.description: Relational test that the item tends to make a fact of consequence more or less probable.

findings.name: Relevance to a fact of consequence
findings.description: Records the relevancy analysis without treating relevance as an inherent property of the item and without confusing it with sufficiency of the whole body of evidence.

questions.text: Does this item have any tendency to make the stated fact more or less probable than it would be without the item?
Is the fact to which the item is directed of consequence in determining the host action or decision?
Does probative value depend on a missing condition of fact, such as whether a statement was heard, that must be recorded as conditional relevance?

data_elements.name: Has probative tendency
data_elements.description: Whether the item tends to change the probability of the fact.

data_elements.name: Probability direction
data_elements.description: More probable or less probable.

data_elements.name: Is of consequence
data_elements.description: Whether the fact is of consequence in determining the action.

data_elements.name: Conditional relevance
data_elements.description: Optional condition of fact on which relevancy depends.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Relevance is a recorded relation and legal-reasoning analysis, not an exhibit.

layers.name: Certainty and statistics
layers.description: Machine-interpretable certainty ratings and the statistics they qualify.

findings.name: Certainty or quality rating
findings.description: Overall and subcomponent certainty using a named system such as GRADE high, moderate, low or very low, with domains, raters and documented reasons for each downgrade or upgrade.

questions.text: What overall certainty, confidence or quality rating is assigned, in which rating system, and with which definition of the category?
Which certainty domains were explicitly considered, including risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, publication bias, large effects, dose-response and residual opposing bias?
Who rated the certainty, was more than one rater used, and when was the rating observed as distinct from the study event time?

data_elements.name: Overall rating
data_elements.description: Overall certainty or quality code.

data_elements.name: Rating system
data_elements.description: Named structured rating system, for example GRADE.

data_elements.name: Domain ratings
data_elements.description: Subcomponent certainty concepts and ratings.

data_elements.name: Raters
data_elements.description: Agents who assigned the certainty rating.

data_elements.name: Rated at
data_elements.description: Timestamp of the rating observation.

artifacts.name: Evidence profile or summary-of-findings table
artifacts.description: GRADE evidence table presenting synthesis results and certainty assessments.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Review or guideline identifier plus table version serial.

findings.name: Quantitative statistic support
findings.description: The numeric heart of scientific evidence: statistic type, quantity, unit, sample size, intervals, p values, model characteristics, and study or synthesis type.

questions.text: What statistic type, quantity, unit of measure and sample size are reported for this evidence bit?
What confidence intervals, p values, heterogeneity estimates and statistic-model characteristics qualify the quantity?
From what study type, and if synthesized from what synthesis type, was the statistic obtained?

data_elements.name: Statistic
data_elements.description: Machine-interpretable statistic backbone including quantity and type.

data_elements.name: Quantity
data_elements.description: Numeric result of the statistic.

data_elements.name: Sample size
data_elements.description: Sample size associated with the statistic.

data_elements.name: Study type
data_elements.description: Type of study from which the evidence was obtained.

data_elements.name: Synthesis type
data_elements.description: Type of synthesis if the evidence is derived from synthesis.

data_elements.name: Variable definitions
data_elements.description: Population, exposure, outcome and other variable roles the statistic is about.

artifacts.name: Statistic payload
artifacts.description: Computable statistic object matching a single combination of variable definitions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Evidence resource identifier plus statistic index.

bundles.name: Authenticity, integrity and custody
bundles.description: Foundations for relying that the item is what it is claimed to be, has not been silently altered, and has a documented handling chronology.
bundles.rationale: Rule 901 requires authentication; C2PA and Verifiable Credentials bind content with hashes and timestamps; ISO/IEC 27037 and NIST SP 800-86 require documented handling so integrity can later be asserted.

layers.name: Authenticity and integrity
layers.description: Authentication foundation and tamper-evident content binding.

findings.name: Authentication foundation
findings.description: The proponent must produce support sufficient to find that the item is what it is claimed to be, using one or more recognized methods such as witness knowledge, distinctive characteristics, public-record custody, or process-or-system accuracy.

questions.text: What is the item claimed to be, and what would count as it being that thing?
Which authentication method or methods are offered, and are they examples under a governing rule or another statute-provided method?
Has authentication been distinguished from later bars such as hearsay, privilege or prejudice that can still exclude an authenticated item?

data_elements.name: Claimed identity of item
data_elements.description: What the proponent claims the item is.

data_elements.name: Authentication methods
data_elements.description: Non-exclusive methods used to authenticate or identify the item.

data_elements.name: Authentication status
data_elements.description: Whether a sufficient foundation has been recorded.

data_elements.name: Remaining bars
data_elements.description: Noted bars that authentication does not remove.

artifacts.name: Authentication foundation record
artifacts.description: Record of the method and supporting testimony or system description used to authenticate the item.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item master identifier plus authentication-event serial.

findings.name: Integrity digest and content binding
findings.description: Hashes, manifests, timestamps and validation states that show the support content has not been tampered with, without converting those proofs into the evidence itself.

questions.text: What digest or data-hash binds the evidence content, with which algorithm, and over which bytes or regions?
What signed claim, C2PA manifest or PROV bundle wraps the assertions, and what is the signer identity used for trust assessment?
What validation state results from checking signature, timestamp, revocation and content hash, without issuing a good-or-bad value judgment about the asset?

data_elements.name: Content digest
data_elements.description: Integrity digest of the evidence file or asset.

data_elements.name: Hash algorithm
data_elements.description: Algorithm used to compute the binding hash.

data_elements.name: Manifest or bundle identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the C2PA manifest or PROV bundle that is itself an entity.

data_elements.name: Signer identity
data_elements.description: Identity of the signer associated with the signing credential.

data_elements.name: Validation state
data_elements.description: Result of the defined validation process.

data_elements.name: Trusted timestamp
data_elements.description: Time-stamp used so signatures can be validated after credential expiry.

artifacts.name: Content credential or integrity manifest
artifacts.description: Signed manifest or claim wrapping assertions and hashes bound to the asset.
artifacts.identity_strategy: C2PA manifest unique identifier or PROV bundle identifier.

layers.name: Chain of custody
layers.description: Chronology of movement and handling needed to later assert integrity.

findings.name: Custody chronology
findings.description: Who handled the item, when, how, under what authorization, and what was done, from identification through later transfers, so custody can be accounted through analysis.

questions.text: Who held or handled the item in each custody interval, and at what event time versus ingestion time?
What transfer, acquisition or handling action occurred, under what authorization, and with what tools or methods?
Was a hash or integrity check verified at intake and at each transfer, and what was the result?

data_elements.name: Custody events
data_elements.description: Ordered handling and transfer events.

data_elements.name: Custodian
data_elements.description: Agent responsible during a custody interval.

data_elements.name: Handling action
data_elements.description: Identification, collection, acquisition, preservation, examination, transfer or similar action.

data_elements.name: Authorization
data_elements.description: Authority under which the handling action was performed.

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: When the handling event occurred, RFC 3339 with offset.

data_elements.name: Ingested at
data_elements.description: When the custody event was recorded in the adopting system.

artifacts.name: Chain-of-custody log
artifacts.description: Chronological log of movement and handling of the potential evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Item master identifier plus monotonic custody-event serial.

bundles.name: Lifecycle and handling
bundles.description: Process states from identification through preservation, publication, challenge, invalidation, sealing, redaction, retention and deletion.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 27037 defines handling activities; FHIR defines publication status; C2PA defines redaction of assertions; PROV defines invalidation of entities.

layers.name: Handling process
layers.description: Identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of potential evidence.

findings.name: Identification, collection, acquisition and preservation
findings.description: Records the handling stage, method, minimization of alteration, and whether the item is still potential evidence versus committed support.

questions.text: Is the item in identification, collection, acquisition, preservation, examination, analysis or reporting, and who performed the stage?
What method was used to collect or acquire the item, and how was alteration minimized and documented?
Is the item being prepared for exchange between jurisdictions or disciplinary procedures, and which handling constraints apply?

data_elements.name: Handling stage
data_elements.description: Current handling activity in the digital-evidence process.

data_elements.name: Handling method
data_elements.description: Documented method of identification, collection, acquisition or preservation.

data_elements.name: Performer
data_elements.description: Agent who performed the handling stage.

data_elements.name: Exchange jurisdictions
data_elements.description: Jurisdictions involved in potential evidence exchange.

artifacts.name: Handling process record
artifacts.description: Process documentation for a handling stage, including tools and minimization of alteration.

layers.name: States and disposition
layers.description: Publication status, challenge, invalidation, retention, sealing and redaction.

findings.name: Status, review, challenge and invalidation
findings.description: Publication lifecycle, review and endorsement, plus challenge of support and PROV-style invalidation when the entity should no longer be relied upon as that item.

questions.text: Is the evidence record draft, active, retired or unknown, and when was it approved or last reviewed?
Who authored, edited, reviewed or endorsed the content, and is the record still fit to mix into a host?
Has the support been challenged, withdrawn, superseded or invalidated, and at what event time did that occur?

data_elements.name: Publication status
data_elements.description: draft, active, retired or unknown.

data_elements.name: Approval date
data_elements.description: When the summary was approved by the publisher.

data_elements.name: Last review date
data_elements.description: When the summary was last reviewed.

data_elements.name: Challenge status
data_elements.description: Whether support is unchallenged, challenged, withdrawn or superseded.

data_elements.name: Invalidated at
data_elements.description: Time the evidence entity was invalidated.

artifacts.name: Status and challenge record
artifacts.description: Lifecycle events including review, endorsement, challenge and invalidation.

findings.name: Retention, sealing and redaction
findings.description: How long support is kept, when it may be deleted, and how assertions or sensitive bodies are redacted without silently rewriting history.

questions.text: What retention period, legal hold or deletion trigger applies to this support record and its artifacts?
Have assertions or bodies been redacted, by whom, under what rights rule, and is the redaction itself signed or manifested?
Is the record sealed against further patch, and what integrity rule prevents silent overwrite of hashes or custody events?

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration or policy reference for keeping the support.

data_elements.name: Legal hold
data_elements.description: Whether deletion is blocked by a hold.

data_elements.name: Redactions
data_elements.description: Recorded redactions of assertions or bodies.

data_elements.name: Rights statement
data_elements.description: Use, publishing or rights restriction on the content.

data_elements.name: Sealed
data_elements.description: Whether the integrity-bound record is sealed against mutation of hashed bytes.

artifacts.name: Redaction or disposition record
artifacts.description: Manifested redaction, seal or disposal event that preserves prior hashes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Original manifest or record id plus redaction serial.

bundles.name: Governance, access and interoperability
bundles.description: Who may create, rely on, disclose or exchange support, and how related artifacts and selectors connect this mixin to other models.
bundles.rationale: FHIR assigns author, publisher, reviewer and endorser roles; Verifiable Credentials and C2PA centre issuer or signer trust; Web Annotation adds rights and selectors; ISO/IEC 27037 contemplates cross-jurisdiction exchange.

layers.name: Stewardship and roles
layers.description: Publishers, authors, issuers, custodians and endorsers.

findings.name: Stewardship, authorship and responsibility
findings.description: Agents bearing responsibility for generating, publishing, attributing, reviewing or holding the support, including delegation.

questions.text: Who is the publisher or steward, and who owns the record in the adopting Dimension?
Which agents authored, issued, or are attributed as responsible, and did any agent act on behalf of another?
What use context, purpose, copyright or terms constrain reuse of the support?

data_elements.name: Publisher or steward
data_elements.description: Organization or individual who publishes the evidence summary.

data_elements.name: Authors
data_elements.description: Who authored the content.

data_elements.name: Issuer
data_elements.description: Issuer who included evidence on a credential.

data_elements.name: Attributed agent
data_elements.description: PROV agent to whom the support entity is attributed.

data_elements.name: Copyright
data_elements.description: Use and publishing restrictions.

data_elements.name: Use context
data_elements.description: Context the content is intended to support.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Stewardship is reference data about agents and rights; role assignments are stored inline unless a separate credential is cited.

layers.name: Access, privilege and disclosure
layers.description: Who may read support, what must be minimized, and what must be audited.

findings.name: Access, privilege and data minimization
findings.description: Evidence often contains personal or privileged content. Verifiable Credentials require privacy and data-minimization considerations; C2PA encourages creator control over inclusion of provenance data; annotations carry rights.

questions.text: Who may read the support record, its artifacts, and each layer, and is the default deny-unless-granted?
What personal, privileged or otherwise sensitive elements must be withheld, abstracted or issued as single-use?
Which read, export, redaction and validation events must be audited, and for how long?

data_elements.name: Default access rule
data_elements.description: Default deny or equivalent for evidence content.

data_elements.name: Sensitive elements
data_elements.description: Elements subject to minimization or privilege.

data_elements.name: Privilege claim
data_elements.description: Optional claim that content is privileged or restricted.

data_elements.name: Audited events
data_elements.description: Access events that must leave an audit trail.

artifacts.name: Access and audit policy binding
artifacts.description: Policy binding that names principals, scopes, exceptions and audit requirements for this record.

layers.name: Interoperability and citation
layers.description: Related artifacts, selectors and alignments to external standards without claiming conformance.

findings.name: Related artifacts, citations and selectors
findings.description: Links or citations to associated artifacts, plus selectors that identify the exact segment offered as support, and optional PROV derivation or collection membership.

questions.text: What related artifacts, citations or cite-as references are associated with this support?
If only a portion of a resource is offered as support, which selector type and values identify that segment?
Which external standards is this record aligned to, and which conflicts or non-conformance notes must travel with it?

data_elements.name: Related artifacts
data_elements.description: Links or citations to associated artifacts.

data_elements.name: Cite as
data_elements.description: Citation for this evidence as reference or markdown.

data_elements.name: Selector
data_elements.description: Selector identifying a segment of a target resource.

data_elements.name: Derived from
data_elements.description: Optional PROV-style derivation from another entity.

data_elements.name: Alignments
data_elements.description: Named external standards aligned but not necessarily conformed to.

artifacts.name: Citation and selector set
artifacts.description: Bundle of citations, related-artifact links and selectors that locate support in external resources.

functions.name: Attach support to a host
functions.description: Mix an evidence or rationale record into a host knowledge object, claim, decision or credential by recording identity, target fact, polarity and type.
preconditions: Host entity exists and is allowed to receive this mixin.
Evidence kind is not a cryptographic securing mechanism.
effects: Creates a citeable support record on the host.
Does not by itself authenticate the item or rate certainty.

functions.name: Record rationale and judgments
functions.description: Capture motivation, narrative reasons and optional Evidence to Decision judgments that explain a claim or decision.
preconditions: A host claim or decision exists to explain.
effects: Stores accessible reasons that can be audited independently of the numeric rating.

functions.name: Rate certainty of a body of evidence
functions.description: Assign overall and domain certainty using a named system, with rater identity and documented domain rationales.
preconditions: Statistics or qualitative findings being rated are identified.
effects: Adds a versioned certainty rating; prior ratings remain as history rather than silent overwrite.

functions.name: Authenticate an evidence item
functions.description: Record the foundation that the item is what it is claimed to be, using one or more recognized methods.
preconditions: An item has been identified and offered as support.
effects: Records authentication without implying legal admissibility or absence of other bars.

functions.name: Bind integrity digest or manifest
functions.description: Attach a hash, signed claim or content credential so later validators can detect tampering.
preconditions: Content is in a preservable state.
Hash algorithm is permitted by the adopting policy.
effects: Seals hashed bytes against silent mutation.
Does not assert that the content is true or good.

functions.name: Record a custody or handling event
functions.description: Append a chronological handling event with custodian, action, authorization, event time and ingestion time.
preconditions: Item has been identified as potential or committed evidence.
Event time is RFC 3339 with offset.
effects: Optionally records an integrity check at transfer.

functions.name: Validate integrity and fitness for purpose
functions.description: Check signature, timestamp, revocation and content hash, and separately assess fitness of the support for the intended host use.
preconditions: Integrity binding exists or is explicitly recorded as absent.
effects: Returns validation state without a good-or-bad value judgment on the underlying asset.
Records that cryptographic validity is not relevance or GRADE certainty.

functions.name: Challenge or invalidate support
functions.description: Mark support as challenged, withdrawn, superseded or invalidated and point to successor or grounds.
preconditions: Support record exists and is not already disposed.
effects: Prevents silent continued reliance on invalidated support.

functions.name: Redact, seal or dispose
functions.description: Apply manifested redaction, seal hashed content, or dispose under retention rules while keeping an audit artifact.
preconditions: Legal hold is absent for deletion.
effects: Hides or removes specified content without rewriting historical hashes.

composition.purpose: Attach traceable support and rationale to a knowledge proposition, finding or recorded knowing without replacing the host.
Reuse entity, activity, agent, derivation, time, bundle and invalidation concepts for how support was produced and for provenance of the evidence record itself.
Align identifiers, status, parties, statistics, related artifacts and certainty when the host domain is health or evidence synthesis.
Align typed supporting-information objects and digests attached to claims, while keeping proofs out of this mixin.
Reuse motivation, agents, rights and selectors when support is expressed as a body about a target segment.
Cite tamper-evident manifests as integrity and origin support for media assets without importing C2PA value-judgment refusal as a truth test.
Align identification, collection, acquisition, preservation and cross-jurisdiction exchange for digital items.
Align incident-oriented collection and integrity-preserving examination steps when support arises from IT forensics.

composition.target: US Federal Rules of Evidence 401 and 901
composition.purpose: Align relevance-as-relation and authentication-foundation tests in US federal legal settings; do not claim other jurisdictions conform.

composition.target: GRADE certainty and Evidence to Decision
composition.purpose: Align certainty domains, evidence tables and documented decision criteria when the host is a recommendation or health decision.

owner_package_requirements: Designate an owner or maintainer for WM-XCT-028 in the adopting Dimension, including a contact able to resolve identifier and access disputes.
Declare the host entity types that MAY receive this mixin and forbid attachment to types that would duplicate a sibling Decision, Claim or Provenance model.
Publish a namespace IRI or equivalent governed prefix for evidence and rationale records, distinct from host knowledge identifiers.
Bind a default certainty-rating system, authentication-method vocabulary and handling-stage vocabulary, each marked as alignment not conformance.
Require AGENTS.md at the package root even when storage is MongoDB, MCP or another interface.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Place mixin records under the adopting Dimension namespace plus a stable /xct/evd/ segment, for example https://{dimension}/xct/evd/{id}. Do not reuse host knowledge IRIs. Hashes, dates and exhibit nicknames are not namespace identifiers.

canonicalization_rules: Identity priority is master-system identifier, then governed IRI, then Dimension UUID or ULID; a timestamp is never canonical identity.
Relevance is stored as a relation to a fact of consequence, never as an inherent flag on an isolated item.
Evidence objects and securing proofs are stored in separate fields; a signature is not canonical evidence.
Certainty ratings name the rating system and keep domain rationales; a single undifferentiated score is non-canonical.
Event time and observation or ingestion time are stored separately as RFC 3339 values with seconds and explicit offset or Z.
Custody events are an append-only ordered collection; the canonical chronology is event time, with ingestion time as audit metadata.
patch_rules: Patches to narrative rationale, EtD judgments and certainty ratings create a new versioned rating or memo; they do not silently replace prior judgments.
Hashed bytes, sealed manifests and completed custody events are immutable; corrections are compensating events.
Redaction is a manifested event that hides content and preserves prior hashes, not an in-place edit of history.
Host-link changes that would retarget support to a different fact of consequence require a new support record rather than a silent patch.
Invalidation sets status and timestamp; it does not delete the audit trail.
compatibility_rules: Additive alignment to FHIR Evidence, VC evidence, C2PA, PROV, GRADE or FRE is allowed; claiming conformance requires evidence not present in this mixin alone.
A GRADE high certainty rating is not compatible with an inference of legal admissibility.
A C2PA valid manifest is not compatible with an inference that depicted events are true.
US FRE alignments are regional; other jurisdictions must supply their own relevance and authentication vocabularies.
Unknown evidence types are preserved as typed extension objects rather than coerced into a closed enumeration.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier such as an exhibit number, FHIR Evidence id or VC evidence id.
Governed global identifier or IRI, including C2PA manifest identifiers and credential evidence ids.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or IRI exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event and observation timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; store event time and observation or ingestion time separately.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts append a monotonic integer or ULID serial to the parent support-record identifier, for example {master-id}.custody.{n} or {master-id}.rationale.{n}, never a date-only name.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Integrity-bound artifacts carry a digest or signed manifest; any mutation of hashed bytes requires a new artifact and a custody or redaction event, not an overwrite.

policies: Do not treat cryptographic proofs, C2PA validation success or GRADE high certainty as substitutes for relevance, authentication or legal admissibility.
Preserve chain-of-custody and rating history even when the host claim is retired, redacted or superseded.
Apply data minimization and privilege review before disclosing evidence bodies that may contain personal or restricted content.
Mark every external-standard mapping as alignment unless a Dimension-level conformance assessment is on file.

read: Any principal granted scope on the host may read non-redacted metadata of attached support.
Artifact bodies, unredacted media and custody logs require an explicit evidence-read grant.
Validation results are readable to relying parties without granting write.
create: Only authors, issuers or designated collectors may create a support record on a host they are allowed to modify.
Creating a custody event requires a custodian role on that item.
Creating a certainty rating requires a rater or reviewer role and a named rating system.
update: Narrative and judgment updates write a new version; hashed and sealed fields are not updatable.
Status changes to retired, challenged or invalidated require reviewer or steward authority.
Access-policy updates require the steward and leave an audit event.
delete: Logical delete or disposal is allowed only when no legal hold applies and retention has expired.
Physical deletion of artifacts still requires a disposition record that retains identifiers, digests and authority.
Invalidation is preferred to delete when later audit of reliance is reasonably foreseeable.

roles.name: Steward
responsibilities: Owns the mixin package in the Dimension.
Sets namespace, host-type bindings, default vocabularies and retention policy.

roles.name: Author or issuer
responsibilities: Creates support records, rationale memos and typed evidence objects.
Declares claimed identity of items and cites related artifacts.

roles.name: Custodian
responsibilities: Performs and records identification, collection, acquisition, preservation and transfers.
Verifies integrity at intake and transfer.

roles.name: Rater or reviewer
responsibilities: Assigns certainty ratings with domain rationales.
Reviews and endorses evidence summaries before they become active.

roles.name: Relying party or verifier
responsibilities: Validates integrity bindings and assesses fitness for a stated purpose.
Must not convert validation success into a truth or admissibility ruling.

roles.name: Redactor or privacy officer
responsibilities: Applies manifested redaction, privilege and minimization.
Authorizes exceptions to default deny for disclosure.

access.default_rule: Deny read of evidence bodies, custody logs and unredacted media unless a principal has an explicit grant; metadata may be visible to host readers if the Dimension so configures.
exceptions: Compulsory legal process or documented safety disclosure may override default deny, and must itself be recorded as an access event with authority and time.
The original author or issuer may read their own unredacted submissions unless a higher privilege or safety hold applies.
Redacted views may be served to a wider audience when a manifested redaction exists.
audit_requirements: Record who read, exported, validated, rated, transferred, redacted or disposed of support, with event time and ingestion time.
Retain audit events at least as long as the support record and its legal holds.
Validation and rating events must capture the policy or rating-system version used.

coverage.claim: This mixin captures the defensible operating surface for traceable support of a claim or decision by unioning primary standards for scientific evidence, credential supporting information, annotation motivation, legal relevance and authentication, content-integrity manifests, and digital-evidence handling, while treating each as alignment rather than universal conformance.

checklist.notes: Master identifier, optional IRI, Dimension UUID or ULID, typed class and business version are modelled; dates are excluded as identifiers.
FHIR publication status, ISO/IEC 27037 handling stages, challenge, invalidation, sealing, redaction and disposition are modelled.
Host mixin link, fact of consequence, polarity, related artifacts, annotation target and optional PROV derivation are modelled.
Event time versus observation or ingestion time, last-changed, approval and review dates, custody intervals and trusted timestamps are modelled using RFC 3339 for instants.
PROV agents, activities, derivation, bundles and C2PA signed claims are aligned as how-produced context, distinct from relevance and certainty.
Publisher, steward, issuer, attributed agent, custodian and copyright or rights statements are modelled.
Authentication foundation, digest binding, C2PA validation states and fitness-for-purpose assessment are modelled as separate checks.
Default deny for bodies, scopes at bundle through artifact, privilege, minimization and audit of read and disclosure are modelled.
Retention period, legal hold, manifested redaction, seal and disposition-with-audit are modelled.
Alignments to FHIR, VC, PROV, C2PA, Annotation, ISO/IEC 27037, NIST SP 800-86, FRE and GRADE are explicit; conformance is not claimed.
FRE 401 relational test and conditional relevance are modelled as first-class operating questions.
GRADE domains, four-level ratings, raters and FHIR certainty plus statistics are modelled.
Chronology of handling with authorization, tools and integrity checks at transfer is modelled from ISO/IEC 27037 and NIST SP 800-86.
Motivation, narrative, notes and Evidence to Decision judgments with opposing considerations are modelled from GRADE, FHIR and Web Annotation.
Physical exhibit location, scene geometry and mobile-device location at acquisition are not specified by the fetched primary texts beyond generic handling location.

known_omissions: No primary Toulmin, IBIS, QOC or Argument Interchange Format schema was fetched; argument-graph interchange is therefore a gap rather than a canonical layer.
ISO/IEC 27042 analysis, ISO/IEC 27043 process architecture and ISO/IEC 17025 laboratory competence were not incorporated as fetched primaries.
Federal Rules 403, 702, 801-807 and 902, and non-US evidence codes, are not modelled; prejudice, expert qualification, hearsay and self-authentication remain legal-sibling concerns.
EDRM e-discovery, CASE/UCO cyber-investigation ontology, STIX opinion/sighting and OMG DMN knowledge sources were not fetched as primaries.
Bayesian likelihood ratios, evidence of absence, and statistical sampling designs as first-class objects are omitted.
Oral testimony capture, real-time live-video evidence beyond C2PA live-video clauses, and AI-generated-content admissibility tests are emerging and under-specified here.
Privilege, work-product and classified-information doctrines lack a single global primary and are represented only as access exceptions.
conflicts: FRE relevance is a low relational bar and is not the same as GRADE certainty of a body of evidence or FHIR statistical quality.
W3C Verifiable Credentials treat evidence as supporting information and treat proofs as a different mechanism; collapsing them would contradict SRC-003.
C2PA forbids value judgments about whether provenance is good or bad, while GRADE and legal triers must make graded or admissibility judgments.
NIST SP 800-86 is explicitly an IT and incident-response view, not a law-enforcement forensic standard, and must not be cited as courtroom procedure.
ISO/IEC 27037 addresses potential digital evidence handling, not scientific evidence synthesis or credential issuance.
US FRE alignments do not travel as global law; treating them as universal would be a false conformance claim.
regional_assumptions: Legal relevance and authentication examples use United States Federal Rules of Evidence as published via LII; other jurisdictions need local mapping.
GRADE is globally used in health guidelines but remains health-originated; non-health decisions must not assume GRADE categories without a documented profile.
ISO/IEC 27037:2012 remains current after 2018 confirmation but is under review; device examples include obsolete media classes that adopting Dimensions should extend.
Privacy minimization follows W3C VC privacy considerations and C2PA creator-control guidance, not a specific GDPR or sectoral statute.
adversarial_checks: Would a cryptographic proof or C2PA valid state be stored as the evidence itself? If yes, the model is being misused against SRC-003 and SRC-008.
Would a GRADE high rating be treated as legal admissibility or as authentication under Rule 901? If yes, domain conflict is being ignored.
Would a date, hash or exhibit nickname be used as the record identifier? If yes, identity priority is violated.
Would this mixin replace WM-KNW-008 Knowledge or a general provenance graph? If yes, the mixin boundary has been breached.
Would silent overwrite of a certainty rating or custody event be allowed? If yes, patch and integrity rules have failed.
Would depicted-event truth be inferred from content credentials? If yes, C2PA scope is being exceeded.
Would Toulmin or AIF structures be required as canonical without a fetched primary? If yes, a gap is being presented as standard.
